supports: The question tool takes two to four options per question.

quote: EV100 is an exposure value (EV) measured at an ISO sensitivity of 100.
supports: EV100 is an exposure value at ISO 100.

quote: Min Sensitivity: The darkest brightness the camera is allowed to get to, measured in EV100.
supports: Godot's auto exposure adapts within a range measured in EV100.

quote: As Godot favors ease of use by default, physical light units are disabled by default.
supports: Godot uses arbitrary light units unless physical light units are enabled.

quote: HDRP uses Physical Light Units (PLU) for its lighting.
supports: Unity HDRP sets light intensities in physical light units.

quote: By default, the engine uses pixel luminance (cd/m2) for the Max Brightness and Min Brightness settings found in the Post Process Volume.
locator: Extend Default Luminance Range for EV100
supports: Unreal's auto exposure range is in cd/m2 by default.

quote: the default luminance range for auto exposure can be extended to express luminance in EV100
locator: Extend Default Luminance Range for EV100
supports: Unreal's auto exposure range can be expressed in EV100 instead.

quote: If Min Brightness is equal to Max Brightness, auto exposure is disabled.
supports: Equal Min and Max Brightness turn Unreal's auto exposure off.

quote: Exposure: Adjusts the brightness of values before they are provided to the tonemapper.
supports: Exposure is applied before the tone mapper.

quote: Tonemapping modes other than Linear are used to make light and dark areas more homogeneous, while also avoiding clipping of bright highlights.
supports: A tone mapper other than Linear keeps bright highlights from clipping.

quote: A 3D look-up-texture (LUT) can also be used for color correction.
locator: Adjustments, Color correction using a 3D LUT
supports: Colour grading can be applied with a 3D LUT.

quote: Sequencer gives users the ability to create in-game cinematics through its specialized multi-track editor.
supports: Unreal's tool for in-game cinematics is Sequencer.

quote: By creating Level Sequences, adding tracks, and creating keyframes you can manipulate objects, characters, and cameras.
supports: An Unreal cinematic is a Level Sequence with tracks and keyframes.

quote: Disables the Camera Cuts track, causing the sequence to not take control of the camera.
supports: A Level Sequence takes control of the camera through its Camera Cuts track.

quote: The Cine Camera Actor is a specialized Camera Actor with additional settings that replicate real-world film camera behavior.
supports: Unreal's Cine Camera Actor replicates film camera behaviour.

quote: You can use the Filmback, Lens, and Focus settings to create realistic scenes, while adhering to industry standards.
supports: The Cine Camera Actor has Filmback, Lens and Focus settings.

quote: The Movie Render Pipeline is Unreal Engine's offline image sequence and movie rendering solution.
supports: Unreal renders sequences offline to images or movies with the Movie Render Pipeline.

quote: A tool you can use to create presets and scripts to queue render processes and then export high-quality images.
supports: Movie Render Queue queues offline renders from presets.

quote: Use Unity's Timeline to create cinematic content, gameplay sequences, audio sequences, and complex particle effects.
supports: Unity's tool for cinematic content is Timeline.

quote: Each cut-scene, cinematic, or gameplay sequence that you create with Unity's Timeline consists of a Timeline asset and a Timeline instance.
supports: A Unity cutscene is a Timeline asset and a Timeline instance.

quote: Cinemachine solves the complex mathematics and logic of tracking targets, composing, blending, and cutting between shots.
supports: Cinemachine composes, blends and cuts between camera shots in Unity.

quote: To use the Cinemachine package, you must install it separately from the Unity Editor.
supports: Cinemachine is a separate package that the project installs.

quote: The AnimationPlayer node allows you to create anything from simple to complex animations.
supports: Godot builds animations on the AnimationPlayer node.

quote: Godot's animation system isn't restricted to position, rotation, and scale. You can animate any property.
supports: An AnimationPlayer can key any property of a node.

quote: If true, the ancestor Viewport is currently using this camera.
supports: Setting a Camera3D's current property makes the viewport use that camera.

quote: xrWaitFrame throttles the application frame loop in order to synchronize application frame submissions with the display.
supports: xrWaitFrame paces the application's frames to the display.

quote: predictedDisplayPeriod is the XrDuration of the display period for the next application-generated frame, for use in predicting display times beyond the next one.
supports: The frame state carries the display period of the next frame.

quote: The runtime may report a different predictedDisplayPeriod from the hardware
locator: XrFrameState, after the Member Descriptions; the sentence ends 'refresh cycle' (re-fetched 2026-11-17)
supports: The period the runtime reports can differ from the hardware's refresh cycle, so it is read, not assumed.

quote: at least one layer is regularly late to be picked up by the compositor, resulting in a degraded user experience
locator: XR_EXT_performance_settings, notification levels, rendering sub-domain, WARNING (re-fetched 2026-11-17)
supports: Frames late to the compositor degrade the user's experience.

quote: xrEnumerateDisplayRefreshRatesFB enumerates the display refresh rates supported by the current session.
supports: Where the extension exists, the session's supported refresh rates are enumerated, not assumed.

quote: The STAGE reference space is a runtime-defined flat, rectangular space that is empty and can be walked around on.
supports: STAGE is the walkable room-scale space.

quote: The LOCAL reference space establishes a world-locked origin, gravity-aligned to exclude pitch and roll, with +Y up, +X to the right, and -Z forward.
supports: LOCAL is a world-locked, gravity-aligned origin.

quote: If used to represent physical distances (rather than e.g. normalized direction) and not otherwise specified, values must be in meters.
supports: OpenXR distances are in meters.

quote: Action sets are application-defined collections of actions.
supports: Input is designed as actions grouped into action sets.

quote: The xrSuggestInteractionProfileBindings function provides action bindings for a single interaction profile.
supports: Bindings are suggested per interaction profile.

quote: This extension enables applications to locate the individual joints of hand tracking inputs.
supports: Hand tracking is the XR_EXT_hand_tracking extension.

quote: Meta Horizon Store apps must meet or exceed Virtual Reality Check (VRC) guidelines to be considered for distribution.
supports: The Meta Horizon Store requires its VRCs.

quote: A plus sign (+) in a column indicates the VRC is a recommendation.
supports: Some VRCs are recommendations, not requirements.

quote: The app must run at the specified refresh rates.
supports: A performance VRC sets the refresh rates; the rates are on the VRC page.

quote: The VRCs listed in these test plans are slightly out of date
supports: The downloadable test plans lag the VRC pages.

quote: The application must respond to the device positional tracking as well as orientation.
supports: A store check needs the app to respond to head tracking.

quote: The results of a compatibility review will not affect whether your game is available to customers on Frame, but will affect how it is presented.
supports: Steam Frame's standalone review rates a game; it does not gate availability.

quote: The same test criteria apply to both VR titles and non-VR titles.
supports: The Steam Frame criteria are the same for VR and non-VR titles.

quote: Techniques like blinks, snap turns, quick turns, smooth turns, position warps, and teleports help users reorient and move without discomfort.
supports: Turning and teleport techniques are comfort options.

quote: Offer smooth turning as an opt-in feature, tuning speed and acceleration carefully.
supports: Smooth turning is offered as opt-in.

quote: Using vignettes to darken screen edges during movement.
supports: Vignettes during movement are a comfort option.

quote: Users have different physical needs and comfort triggers. Test your application with diverse users and offer customizable locomotion options.
supports: Comfort options are customizable and tested with diverse users.

quote: Vection is a visually induced phenomenon that occurs during slide locomotion in VR, where the user perceives movement through visual cues even when physically stationary.
supports: Vection is the comfort risk of slide locomotion.

quote: glTF uses a right-handed coordinate system. glTF defines +Y as up, +Z as forward, and -X as right;
supports: glTF 2.0 is right-handed with +Y up and +Z forward.

quote: The units for all linear distances are meters. All angles are in radians.
supports: glTF 2.0 linear distances are in meters.

quote: Each skin is defined by a REQUIRED joints property that lists the indices of nodes used as joints to pose the skin
supports: A glTF skin lists the joints that pose it.

quote: The order of joints is defined by the skin.joints array and it MUST match the order of inverseBindMatrices accessor elements
supports: The joint order must match the inverse bind matrices.

quote: When any of the vertices are influenced by more than four joints, the additional joint and weight information are stored in subsequent sets.
supports: glTF stores four joint influences per set; more go into further sets.

quote: When the weights are stored using float component type, their linear sum SHOULD be as close as reasonably possible to 1.0 for a given vertex.
supports: A vertex's float skin weights sum to one.

quote: An altered state of a mesh primitive defined as a set of difference values for its vertex attributes.
supports: A glTF morph target (a blendshape) is a set of difference values.

quote: the primitives' attributes are obtained by adding the original attributes to a weighted sum of the target’s attributes.
supports: A morphed mesh adds a weighted sum of target offsets to the base.

quote: The stage up axis is encoded as stage metadatum upAxis, whose legal values are "Y" and "Z"
supports: OpenUSD's upAxis is stage metadata, Y or Z.

quote: Exporters, however, are strongly encouraged to always set the upAxis for every USD file they create.
supports: Exporters should always author upAxis.

quote: Like OpenGL and the fallback for UsdGeomGprim::GetOrientationAttr(), UsdGeom stipulates a right-handed coordinate system.
supports: UsdGeom is right-handed.

quote: If unauthored, will return the value provided by UsdGeomGetFallbackUpAxis().
supports: An unauthored upAxis reads as the fallback.

quote: declaring a site-level fallback up axis (UsdGeomGetFallbackUpAxis()) that can be configured with a PlugPlugin plugInfo.json file.
supports: The fallback up axis is a per-site setting.

quote: We encode linear measure as meters per unit (stage-level metadata metersPerUnit) rather than units-per-meter
supports: OpenUSD's metersPerUnit is stage metadata.

quote: If a UsdStage has no authored metersPerUnit we fall back to the value UsdGeomLinearUnits::centimeters, i.e. 0.01.
supports: An unauthored metersPerUnit falls back to centimeters (0.01).

quote: Return whether stage has an authored metersPerUnit.
supports: An importer can tell whether metersPerUnit was authored.

quote: usdchecker attempts to validate a USD or usdz file using a series of rules and metrics that will evolve over time.
supports: usdchecker validates a USD or usdz file.

quote: Describes a target blend shape, possibly containing inbetween shapes.
supports: A UsdSkel BlendShape is a target shape with optional inbetweens.

quote: To bind blend shapes, the skel:blendShapeTargets rel should be created, and set to target UsdSkelBlendShape primitives, which define each shape.
supports: UsdSkel binds blend shapes through skel:blendShapeTargets.

quote: Tool to validate glTF assets.
supports: glTF-Validator validates glTF assets.

quote: Validator writes a validation report (in JSON-format) with all found issues and asset stats.
supports: glTF-Validator writes a JSON report of the issues it finds.

quote: This class represents the coordinate system of the scene and can convert scenes to other coordinate systems.
supports: An FBX scene carries its own axis system.

quote: It determines if the axis system is right-handed or left-handed just as the enum values.
supports: FBX handedness is part of the scene's axis system.

quote: This class describes the units of measurement used within a particular scene.
supports: An FBX scene carries its own unit.

quote: Returns the scene's current coordinate system.
supports: The axis system is read from the scene's global settings.

quote: Returns the unit of measurement used by the system.
supports: The unit is read from the scene's global settings.

quote: For example, JOINTS_1 and WEIGHTS_1 if present will reference the accessor for up to 4 additional joints that influence the vertices.
supports: Influences beyond the first four go into JOINTS_1 and WEIGHTS_1.

quote: LOCAL space is useful when an application needs to render seated-scale content that is not positioned relative to the physical floor
locator: 14.4.1 XR_EXT_local_floor, Overview (extension promoted to OpenXR 1.1; re-fetched 2026-11-17)
supports: LOCAL is for seated-scale content, not positioned relative to the floor.

quote: The STAGE space is useful when an application needs to render standing-scale content (no bounds) or room-scale content (with bounds)
supports: Standing-scale content uses STAGE without bounds; room-scale uses STAGE with bounds.

quote: However, the origin of this space is defined to be on an estimate of the floor level. Runtimes must support LOCAL_FLOOR reference space.
locator: 7.1 Reference Spaces, XR_REFERENCE_SPACE_TYPE_LOCAL_FLOOR (provided by XR_VERSION_1_1; re-fetched 2026-11-17)
supports: LOCAL_FLOOR is core in OpenXR 1.1, every runtime supports it, and its origin is on an estimate of the floor level.

quote: Support for the STAGE reference space is optional
supports: A runtime may offer no stage, so the design needs a fallback.

quote: The minimum sensitivity (in ISO) used when calculating auto exposure.
supports: CameraAttributesPractical's Min Sensitivity is in ISO.

quote: The maximum sensitivity (in ISO) used when calculating auto exposure.
supports: CameraAttributesPractical's Max Sensitivity is in ISO.

quote: The minimum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure.
supports: CameraAttributesPhysical's auto exposure minimum is in EV100.

quote: The maximum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure.
supports: CameraAttributesPhysical's auto exposure maximum is in EV100.
